card.statement:
[<<cite:h-s_unit>>]
Let $A$ be
a square complex
matrix such that $A^2$
is normal. Then $A$ is
unitarily similar to

- [(a)]
a direct sum of
blocks, each of which
is

\begin{equation}
\begin{bmatrix} \lambda
\end{bmatrix}\ \text{ or
}\
\begin{bmatrix}
\mu & r\\ 0&-\mu
\end{bmatrix},\qquad
\begin{matrix}
\lambda,\mu\in\mathbb
C,\
0\le \arg(\mu)<\pi,\\
r\in\mathbb R,\ r>0;
\end{matrix}
\end{equation}

and

- [(b)]
to a direct sum of
blocks, each of which
is

\begin{equation}
\begin{bmatrix} \lambda
\end{bmatrix}\ \text{ or
}\
\tau\!\begin{bmatrix}
0 & 1\\ \nu&0
\end{bmatrix}
,\qquad
\begin{matrix}
\lambda, \nu \in
\mathbb C,\ |\nu|<1,\\
\tau\in \mathbb R,\
\tau>0.
\end{matrix}
\end{equation}

These direct sums are
uniquely determined by
$A$, up to permutation
of summands.
Conversely, if $A$ is
unitarily similar to a
direct sum of blocks
of the form <<ref:s1>>
or <<ref:s2>>, then
$A^2$ is normal.
card.label: Theorem 1

paper.title: Classification of squared normal operators on unitary and Euclidean spaces
paper.abstract: We give a canonical form for a complex matrix, whose square is normal, under transformations of unitary similarity as well as a canonical form for a real matrix, whose square is normal, under transformations of orthogonal similarity.
